newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pakhoed H1 soars, raises 1997 forecast.
newsitem.headline: Pakhoed H1 soars, raises 1997 forecast.

text.p: Dutch tank storage and shipping group Pakhoed NV said on Wednesday its net profit from ordinary operations rose by 75 percent to about 103 million guilders in the first half of 1997.
First-half net attributable to holders of ordinary shares was about 96 million guilders or some 3.00 guilders per share, compared with 1.91 guilders in the year-ago period
Pakhoed said it now expected a full-year 1997 attributable net profit in the range of 170 to 180 million guilders or 5.31 to 5.62 guilders per ordinary share.
In 1996, the company posted a total full-year net from ordinary operations of 138.3 million guilders and an attributable net of 75.5 million guilders.

Pakhoed said the strong profit rise in the first half of the current year was mainly caused by continuously higher results at its U.S. chemicals distribution unit, a positive contribution from oil storage activities in Rotterdam and favourable currency rate effects.
Because of these developments, it had raised its full-year forecast, Pakhoed said. The firm previously said it expected profits to show double-digit growth in 1997.
Pakhoed said it will publish a full statement on its first-half results on August 20.
